summary: Jongcheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2001).

Jongmyung Kim works in Buddhist and religious studies and history. He studied at Yonsei University, Seoul National University, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He served as Associate Professor of Korean Buddhism at the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2012–2019).

Joryu Chiba was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology who studied at Ryukoku University. He spent his career primarily at Ryukoku University (1950–1989) and led institutions including the Honganji Historical Materials Research Institute and Shinshu Institute of Doctrinal Studies.

Jos Gommans is a historian and Indologist who studied at Radboud University Nijmegen and Leiden University, where he completed his doctoral studies under Jan C. Heesterman and André Wink. He was appointed associate professor at Leiden University in 1993.
Josef Horovitz was a scholar of religious studies and history who completed his doctoral studies under Eduard Sachau. He served on the faculty at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1914 to 1931.

Josef Schick was a linguist who studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he earned his PhD in 1889. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and the University of Munich, where he was professor from 1896 to 1925.

Josef Strzygowski was an art historian who studied at the University of Munich. He held academic posts at the University of Graz (~1892–1909), the University of Vienna (~1909–1933), and Åbo Akademi University (~1920–1923).
Josef van Ess was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Bonn from around 1953 to 1959. He held a post at the University of Tübingen from around 1968 to 1999.

Joseph Campbell was a scholar of religious studies who studied at Dartmouth, Columbia University, the University of Paris, and the University of Munich. He held a post at Sarah Lawrence College from 1934 to 1972.
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his Master of Arts at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).
Joseph Dalton Hooker studied at the University of Glasgow (~1832–1839). He served at the British Geological Survey (1845–1847) and as Director of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew (1847–1885).

Joseph E. Schwartzberg was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Brooklyn College, the University of Maryland, the Sorbonne, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne. He served as professor at the University of Minnesota from 1964 to 2000.

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion who studied at University College School and the University of London. He served as President of Harris Manchester College, Oxford, and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1889–1915).

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies and religious teacher who studied at Columbia University and under traditional teachers including Anagarika Munindra and Dipa Ma. He taught at Naropa University in 1974 and co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Joseph Hackin was an archaeologist and scholar of Asian studies who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot in Paris. He served as curator at the Guimet Museum (1913–1941) and directed the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan beginning in 1934.

Joseph Haroutunian was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia University and Union Theological Seminary. He held academic posts at Wellesley College, McCormick Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Loizzo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied at Amherst, Harvard, and under Robert A. F. Thurman. He served as a Visiting Scholar of Religion at Columbia University and founded the Nalanda Institute for Contemplative Science.

Joseph M. Kitagawa was a scholar of religion, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Joachim Wach. He spent his career at the University of Chicago from 1951, serving as Dean of the Divinity School.
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who completed his MA at Columbia University. He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University beginning in 1991.

Joseph A. Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox. He was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).
